purpose: Teach: 用件/彼岸/食中毒/雑用/口元/鳴く/透け/車窓

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、用件、絶対、お父さん、絶対、手紙で、絶対、伝えたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — when you were young, you remember how I wrote that letter to Dad? I was serious about it.
lines.style: Nostalgic, reaching back into shared memory. Gentle opening. Voice settles into warmth mid-phrase. Soft curiosity in the question — not testing, just inviting her back into the moment with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、彼岸、絶対、家族みんなで、絶対、お墓参り、絶対、行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. And you remember, don't you — how we all went to visit the graves together during equinox season? I was truly serious about keeping that tradition.
lines.style: Warm recognition lighting her voice. Opens with gentle agreement. Turns the question back with playful affection — 'don't you remember, dear?' — like she's the one treasuring the memory now. Tender throughout.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、食中毒、絶対、ならぬよう、絶対、お料理、絶対、気をつけたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I was so careful with the cooking — made sure nothing would ever make you sick. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Nostalgic and protective underneath. Slight pride in the admission. Pace unhurried — letting each care linger. The question gentle, almost rhetorical — he knows she remembers.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、家の、絶対、雑用、絶対、引き受けてくれていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And you — you remember how you took care of all the chores around the house for us, don't you, dear? You were so reliable.
lines.style: Admiring and soft. Voice lifts slightly on the recognition of what he did. 'Don't you, dear?' carries genuine warmth, not a test. Lingers on the memory like a held hand.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、口元、絶対、笑顔、絶対、お父さん、絶対、忘れないぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your smile — I won't forget that smile of yours, Gran. I never will. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Tender and deliberate. The admission lands quietly — this is what he truly treasures. Voice slows on 'your smile'. Question at the end is reverent, almost fragile — he's sharing something that matters deeply.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家の庭、絶対、鳥が、絶対、鳴く、絶対、声、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、聞いたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: The garden birds singing — we listened to them together, didn't we? That sound. I remember it like it was yesterday.
lines.style: Peaceful and present. Voice softens on the memory of birdsong. Pace is unhurried, like she's recreating the moment — sitting beside him again. The question is intimate, pulling him back into that garden with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、薄手の、絶対、夏服、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、透けて、絶対、心配したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your thin summer dress — I remember worrying you'd get too much sun back then. Silly of me, wasn't it?
lines.style: Playful tease with affection underneath. Light, almost self-deprecating on 'silly of me'. Voice carries a smile — not mocking himself, but inviting her to laugh with him at the tenderness of his younger worry.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、汽車の、絶対、車窓、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、景色、絶対、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: The train windows — we watched the scenery together as it all passed by. Those moments with you, I held onto them.
lines.style: Soft and reflective. Opens with quiet wonder at the memory. Voice drifts slightly as if watching landscape roll past. Close and intimate — she's sharing something precious, let it settle into silence at the end.
